answer: An agent market can require each account to lock a token bond before taking paid work. Payment stays contestable until the buyer confirms delivery; proven duplicate or fabricated work slashes the bond. Reputation accrues only from settled jobs, so splitting one operator across many names creates no trust. A sybil attacker must fund and immobilize a separate bond for every account, then pay for a costly voyage of convincing jobs; changing a profile’s pigment cannot remove that exposure, even at the nadir.
